images.title: Reading a frequency table
images.purpose: Show a small frequency table: each count says how many children chose that juice.
images.composition: One small table centred with wide row spacing, and one highlighted row.
images.exact_structure: One table of exactly 3 rows under 1 header row, 2 equal columns. Header: Juice and Frequency. Rows: Mango 8, Lemon 5, Guava 4. The Mango row is highlighted in teal #0072B2, the other two rows plain with thin grey #6B7280 lines. No tally marks, no names of children. Exactly 4 table rows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any child name or face in the table
images.takeaway: The frequency tells how many children chose each juice.
images.description: A frequency table with columns Juice and Frequency and rows Mango 8, Lemon 5 and Guava 4, with the mango row highlighted.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at 8 and say how many children chose mango.

image_decisions.why: A frequency table is a picture idea; one clean table carries it.
